title: What Babies Learn From Spit-Swapping - Nautilus
gist: A study in Evolution and Human Behavior proposes that helpless human infants may identify who will care for them by watching who shares saliva. The research, led by Brandon Woo of UC Santa Barbara, builds on cross-cultural findings that people in close relationships are more comfortable sharing saliva and tests whether 4- to 6-month-olds can read this cue.

insights.claim: Because human babies are born completely helpless and rely on others for food, water and other needs, working out who can be counted on to provide care is especially important for them.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Frames early social cognition as an evolved survival mechanism.
insights.quote: That makes figuring out who can be counted on to provide those things pretty important for the little guys.

insights.claim: A new study in Evolution and Human Behavior suggests infants may identify close relationships, and thus likely caregivers, by observing who swaps saliva.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Points to surprisingly sophisticated relationship inference in pre-verbal infants.
insights.quote: they might accomplish this important goal by watching who swaps spit

insights.claim: Studies across cultures have found that people in close relationships are often more comfortable sharing saliva with each other, which inspired research led by Brandon Woo of the University of California, Santa Barbara.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A cross-cultural behavioural cue that signals relationship closeness.
insights.quote: We were inspired by studies that found that across cultures, people in close relationships are often more comfortable sharing saliva with each other

insights.claim: The saliva-sharing study examines whether infants as young as 4 to 6 months old can infer how two people are related from cues such as sharing an ice cream cone.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Sets up a test of how early humans read social bonds.
insights.quote: So imagine seeing two people licking the same ice cream cone—could you guess how they might know each other?
